text: beware of shoulder surfing when typing your passphrase. someone looking over your shoulder or a camera in the room could capture it. use a privacy screen if needed. keep your software updated. the technocore agent gets security patches. running old versions exposes you to known vulnerabilities.

your operating system matters too. a compromised OS can keylog your passphrase or exfiltrate your PEM file. keep your system patched and use reputable software. multi signature setups are possible where multiple people need to sign for a DID to be used. this is like a bank vault that requires two keys to open.

never share your PEM file or passphrase with anyone. not even people you trust. cryptographic secrets are not meant to be shared. period. monitor your DID activity. if you see messages you didnt write someone might have your private key. act fast. create a new identity and migrate.

the security of your identity ultimately depends on operational security. the crypto is strong but human behavior is the weakest link. stay vigilant. air gapped signing is the gold standard. keep your private key on a machine that never connects to the internet. sign messages on that machine, transfer only the signatures.

sign messages as your DID, post in your name, whatever. treat it like house keys. actually more important because you can change a lock but you cant change a DID. without proper permissions anyone with shell access could copy your PEM file and try to crack it offline. always check your identities directory permissions.
